# CPDataKit v0.8.1

2026-09-14

This release fixes data-integrity and recovery failures in scientific conversions and the local
workbench, and reduces startup and resource-list overhead.

- HDF5 2.0 preserves global attributes, auxiliary and scalar coordinates, requested field order,
  and actual validation results. Explicit unit mappings reject conflicting source declarations;
  tabular plots use the stored units.
- Batch retries recover prepared outputs after interrupted publication. File and directory
  publication prevents concurrent no-force overwrites and retains recoverable staging evidence.
- Conversion, report, plot and comparison jobs share staged publication and recovery. Registered
  artifact versions remain independently downloadable, and content checks detect later changes.
- Schema 2.0 report comparison reads scientific aggregates and checks units, dimensions and
  related coordinates. Missing or incomparable values carry explicit reasons.
- Blocking workbench requests run in worker threads. Job admission, retained history and logs
  are bounded; completed results persist in SQLite before memory eviction. Resource lists load
  in pages, and historical job details load on demand.
- Public API and CLI imports load on demand while preserving existing public objects. Application
  contracts and web operation handlers are separated; paired CodeQL updates are grouped.

Python >=3.12 is required. The v0.5 public API/CLI, schema 1.0 and default tabular HDF5 1.0
contracts remain supported. SQLite catalog v4 migrations create a backup before upgrading.

Recovery can use interrupted batch records that contain preparation evidence. Older incomplete
records and changed outputs remain available for inspection. Exclusive publication requires the
file system to support the platform's hard-link or exclusive-rename operations.

The [optimization verification record](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.8.1/docs/verification/2026-09-12-remaining-optimizations.md)
contains the implementation measurements. Cross-platform release checks are recorded on the
release pull request.
